walkthrough:
Express the gradients of segments $PR$ and $QR$ in terms of $k$:
$$m_{PR} = \frac{k - 5}{2 - (-13)} = \frac{k - 5}{15}, \quad m_{QR} = \frac{k - 1}{2 - 5} = \frac{k - 1}{-3}$$

Since $\angle PRQ = 90^\circ$, the lines are perpendicular ($m_{PR} \times m_{QR} = -1$):
$$\left(\frac{k - 5}{15}\right)\left(\frac{k - 1}{-3}\right) = -1 \implies \frac{(k - 5)(k - 1)}{-45} = -1 \implies (k - 5)(k - 1) = 45$$

Expand and rearrange into standard quadratic form:
$$k^2 - 6k + 5 = 45 \implies k^2 - 6k - 40 = 0$$

Factorise the quadratic to find the values of $k$:
$$(k - 10)(k + 4) = 0 \implies k = 10 \quad\text{or}\quad k = -4$$

ai_rubric.Perpendicular Lines: Forms $m_{PR}=\frac{k-5}{15}$ and $m_{QR}=\frac{k-1}{-3}$, sets product to $-1$, and solves $k^2-6k-40=0$ to find $k=10, -4$.

hints: Find the centre $C$ as the midpoint of diameter $PQ$: $C(-4, 3)$.
Use the perpendicular tangent gradient $m_{\text{tangent}} = -\frac{6}{7}$ at $R(2, 10)$ to form $6x + 7y - 82 = 0$.
walkthrough:
Since $\angle PRQ = 90^\circ$, $PQ$ is the diameter of the circle; find the centre $C$ as the midpoint of $PQ$:
$$C = \left(\frac{-13 + 5}{2},\ \frac{5 + 1}{2}\right) = (-4, 3)$$

Calculate the gradient of the radius $CR$ connecting centre $C(-4, 3)$ and $R(2, 10)$:
$$m_{\text{radius}} = \frac{10 - 3}{2 - (-4)} = \frac{7}{6}$$

Find the perpendicular gradient of the tangent line ($m_{\text{tangent}} \times m_{\text{radius}} = -1$):
$$m_{\text{tangent}} = -\frac{6}{7}$$

Write the equation of the tangent line at $R(2, 10)$ in integer form $ax + by + c = 0$:
$$y - 10 = -\frac{6}{7}(x - 2) \implies 7(y - 10) = -6(x - 2) \implies 7y - 70 = -6x + 12 \implies 6x + 7y - 82 = 0$$

ai_rubric.Equations of Tangents to Circles: Finds centre $(-4,3)$, radius gradient $\frac{7}{6}$, tangent gradient $-\frac{6}{7}$, and rearranges to $6x + 7y - 82 = 0$.
